items.title: DJI’s Osmo Pocket 3 vlogging camera is a good deal at under $400
items.raw:
DJI’s Osmo Pocket 3 is a big upgrade from your phone’s video quality.﻿ | Image: The Verge	

If you’re the kind of person who likes to document everything, either for professional and/or personal reasons, and your phone’s camera isn’t cutting it, you might be considering a dedicated vlogging camera. The DJI Osmo Pocket 3 is discounted to $395 (usually $499) at a variety of retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, and B&H Photo. The large 1-inch sensor is mounted to a built-in gimbal that offers smooth, stable movement, letting you take impressive videos of your travels, activities, or daily routine. The built-in screen helps you frame shots and check footage on the go without pulling out your phone.
DJI Osmo Pocket 3
The Pocket 3 features a 1-inch CMOS sensor, three built-in microphones, and a 2-inch rotatable screen. If you’re unhappy with the video your phone captures, DJI’s compact cam makes it easy to get high-quality, stabilized footage, whether you’re vlogging your adventures or filming a wedding. Read our impressions.

Where to Buy:

 $499 $395 at Amazon
 $499 $395 at Best Buy
 $499 $395 at B&H Photo

The Pocket 3, like its name implies, is compact enough to easily slide into a pocket or small bag, yet still manages to take high quality video. The results are often compared to pricier dedicated mirrorless digital cameras, delivered without the fuss of tweaking exposure or heavy post-processing. It’s capable of shooting up to 4K at 120 frames per second, and while it has built-in microphones, you can connect it to DJI’s Mic Mini wireless mics. While there is a DJI Osmo Pocket 4, it isn’t officially for sale in the United States.
Read our DJI Osmo Pocket 3 review.
Other deals to consider
You can save $10 on your preorder of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort for the Switch 2 at Amazon, bringing the price down to just $49.94, effectively letting you grab the physical release for the same price as the digital version. This title brings back all the minigames from the original Wii title, including bowling and tennis, plus a new open-world mode that introduces activities like skateboarding, and ships out on October 22nd, 2026. Read our review.
The Glorious GMMK 2 mechanical gaming keyboard is steeply discounted at Best Buy, bringing the price down to $48.99 (originally $119.99). The compact 65 percent layout includes just the primary letters and numbers, plus arrow keys and few spares for the delete, page up, page down, and end keys. The kit includes Glorious Fox linear switches, but with hot-swappable sockets, you can easily change them out to suit your preference.
Keep your Qi-ready devices topped up with a discounted two-pack of Anker Zolo MagSafe-compatible wireless chargers at Amazon for $25.99 (usually $39.99). These chargers have five foot cables with USB-C ports, so you’ll need to supply the wall charger, and support up to 15W of charging power on Qi2-compatible devices.

items.title: Amazon is phasing out Fire HD tablets, but not without some big discounts first
items.raw:
The Fire HD 10 offers a sharper, larger screen than its smaller siblings. | Image: Amazon	

Amazon recently announced it’s phasing out its Fire HD tablets in favor of much pricier Alexa Tablets. While the days of getting an affordable, but good tablet from Amazon seem to be coming to an end, you can still get a fantastic deal on the ad-supported Amazon Fire HD 10. It has dropped to a new low of $72.99 ($82 off) at Amazon. While it’s far from the fastest tablet out there, it’s a solid option for watching movies, reading books, or browsing the web. And, it’ll continue to get security updates.
Amazon Fire HD 10 (2023)

Where to Buy:

 $139.99 $72.99 at Amazon (32GB, with ads)

The Fire HD 10 is one of the nicer models in Amazon’s budget-friendly Fire lineup, and at its current price, is actually slightly cheaper than the Fire HD 8. The Fire HD 10 offers a spacious, sharper 10.1-inch 1080p display that makes watching shows and reading more enjoyable than on the Fire HD 8’s smaller, lower-res screen. It also offers better front-facing cameras for video calls and up to 13 hours of battery life, so you don’t need to worry about it dying during long road trips or flights.
If the 32GB of built-in storage isn’t enough, there’s a microSD card slot for expanding it up to 1TB, so you can download more apps, movies, shows, and books for offline use. Plus, Amazon’s tablet has a 3.5mm headphone jack — something you won’t find on newer iPads. If you’re really into smart assistants, the Fire HD 10 supports Alexa Plus, which Prime members can access for free. Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant can handle more complex requests and is particularly useful for managing your smart home, though we’ve had mixed results with other tasks.
You may be aware that the Fire HD 10 runs Amazon’s Fire OS rather than Android (the new Alexa Tablets support Google Play Store out of the box). However, it’s possible to sideload Android apps onto it with relative ease, though keep in mind that the Fire HD 10’s low-end specs might mean that your favorite Android apps and games might not run all that well.

items.title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan
items.raw:
DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.
Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.

items.title: Israeli police detain 10 people in rare raid against West Bank settlers

Move comes after US photojournalist and group of European diplomats and Palestinians were assaulted in separate attacks
Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist Heidi Levine, which she described as an “attempted lynching”.
She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked Israeli men as she covered the olive harvest in a Palestinian village on Friday. The militants broke four vertebrae and a rib, ripped open her finger so it required surgery and left her with lacerations across her body.

items.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
items.raw:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces 
At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.
The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.

items.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
items.raw:
Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece
In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.
Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.

items.title: Three deaths from float crushes raise safety concerns over Japanese festivals
items.raw:
Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere
There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.
Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.

items.raw:
Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearance
A New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.
The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US expedition to the Pacific atoll of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.
